targetEvidence.finding: SSR verifies a session and keeps data params empty by default; signed-out dynamic chat, news-edit, wallet, disable, and plan shells reduce layout paths to static collections so breadcrumbs and return URLs cannot disclose route references; a boundary-aware helper removes exactly one canonical admin mount prefix so repeated prefixes cannot alias an allowlisted loader; payment intents, the admin news list, the redacted global notification inventory, the redacted audit inventory, the news/public media compatibility inventory, the two-count root dashboard snapshot, and the four-count wallet summary perform normalized authenticated reads with explicit ready, empty where applicable, forbidden where applicable, unavailable, or malformed outcomes.

The root-dashboard adapter accepts no query grammar, targets only the new typed admin GET, forwards only a verified admin bearer and request ID, follows no redirects, caps declared and streamed bodies at 256 KiB, strictly decodes the full envelope, and rejects negative, inconsistent, or temporally impossible snapshots. Only observation time plus total and active i64 counts enter SSR state.

anchors: COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE is_active = TRUE)::bigint AS active_users
targetEvidence.finding: The backend performs one snapshot statement against wallet_users, returns only database observation time and two i64 counts, rejects every query string before database access, propagates dependency failure, and fails closed unless both counts are non-negative and active does not exceed total.

The production admin router mounts the new read on an isolated subrouter, applies the exact-admin audience guard outside the dashboard permission guard, and merges that protected subrouter without changing the legacy dashboard group.

JWT audience provenance is retained only in server context and omitted from serialization and deserialization. The selected-route guard accepts exactly one epsx-admin audience, rejects missing context, API-key authentication, frontend/API audiences, and mixed or duplicate audiences with a generic Bearer challenge, and leaves existing routes and permission grammar unchanged.

The page-owned dashboard shell independently validates the exact two-count projection, treats zero as ready, renders a semantic definition list and machine-readable observation time, distinguishes forbidden, unavailable, and malformed outcomes, keeps signed-out data private, and exposes no health, latency, uptime, alert, activity, module, row, identity, or mutation claim.

The active commerce adapters target the wallet stats/detail/credit reads owned by the wallet service, validate canonical wallet parameters, cap serialized responses at 512 KiB, classify unauthorized and dependency failures, strictly decode deny-unknown response DTOs, and project only the safe fields needed by the page. Correlation, metadata, ownership, actor, timestamps, and mutation evidence are discarded before PageContext.

The body-only wallet-list page independently validates the four-count projection, treats zero as ready, distinguishes forbidden, unavailable, and malformed states, and always presents a separate inventory-unavailable notice. Focused Rust tests cover redaction, signed-out privacy, accessible responsive semantics, no nested shell, no rows or identities, and no detail, disable, or other mutation affordance.

The compatibility adapter targets the pinned Rust backend's protected admin-news contract, caps declared and chunked response bodies at 8 MiB before JSON allocation, rejects duplicate or malformed recognized query values and structural or semantic response drift, projects away bodies and identity/media fields for list state, and sends explicit lifecycle actions with backend-owned authorization and optimistic versions. The public file-backed content feed is deliberately not used as admin state.

The admin adapter forwards only a verified bearer and request ID to exact global-list and metrics endpoints, fixes the page size at 20, forwards only bounded status/type/priority filters, caps declared and chunked bodies at 256 KiB, rejects structural and semantic drift, and projects only bounded delivery metadata. Its read/delete actions validate IDs and preserve forbidden, unavailable, and malformed outcomes without forwarding caller identity headers.

anchors: ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT $1 OFFSET $2
SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ, READ ONLY
admin notification inventory contains invalid stored fields
targetEvidence.finding: The notification service owns deterministic global list and metrics reads with strict limit/offset/filter parsing and redacted DTOs. Count and page rows share one read-only repeatable-read transaction, and impossible cardinality, count failures, or invalid stored fields fail closed; read and delete mutations require the canonical admin permission and strict notification IDs.

The direct notification service admits only the exact admin list, metrics, mark-read, and delete shapes after verifying the admin audience and canonical admin:notifications:manage permission; method, arity, ID, and encoded-path drift fail closed before the handler.

The authenticated management page renders only the strict redacted projection with native pagination, typed filters, backend-derived metrics, and server forms for mark-read/delete. It distinguishes ready, authoritative empty, forbidden, unavailable, malformed, and out-of-range recovery without identities, bodies, delivery errors, action URLs, or client-side authorization.

anchors: SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL REPEATABLE READ, READ ONLY
ORDER BY created_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT $4
targetEvidence.finding: The extracted analytics service owns an exact-audience, dedicated-permission read over only the canonical unified audit table. Startup validates the existing table shape, rows use stable keyset continuation in a read-only repeatable-read transaction, invalid stored fields fail the page, and the SELECT/DTO omit identity, target, network/device, before/after, and metadata fields.

The audit BFF adapter accepts only a closed category and bounded canonical cursor, follows no redirects, forwards only the verified bearer and request ID, caps declared and chunked bodies at 256 KiB, binds response rows to the requested category, validates newest-first unique summaries, rejects sensitive or unknown fields, and distinguishes ready, authoritative empty, forbidden, unavailable, and malformed outcomes.

The SSR-only compatibility adapter accepts only the exact news/public bucket subset, calls the protected legacy GET /api/admin/media/{news|public}?limit=100 route with the verified admin bearer, follows no redirects, caps declared and chunked bodies before JSON allocation, and rejects request, status, response-envelope, or semantic drift. It projects only key, size, and optional last-modified time; URLs and private chat/notification bucket keys never cross into PageContext, and dependency or malformed outcomes never become an authoritative empty inventory.

The authenticated media page independently validates the redacted projection and renders explicit ready, authoritative-empty, forbidden, unavailable, and malformed states with native news/public bucket and retry links. It emits only object key, size, and optional timestamp text, while upload/delete forms carry validated actions to the backend; no URL, preview, private bucket, or client-side policy crosses the UI boundary.

The authenticated page independently validates the redacted projection and renders native category/keyset links, responsive labelled summary rows, semantic timestamps, and explicit outcome recovery without rendering record IDs, actor/target identity, details, export, forms, or mutations; the current reversible continuation token still carries the audit UUID and remains an explicit blocker.
The payments proxy is wired to the canonical typed admin-wide intent read; other proxy handlers generally remain disconnected from their page payloads.
The BFF preserves a closed safe status set and explicit dependency classes without forwarding upstream details, but still returns bare statuses rather than a typed error envelope consumed by pages.

The dispatcher validates route shape and extracts dynamic params, and signed-out dynamic chat, news-edit, wallet, disable, and plan skeletons use only static collection return paths so route references are not disclosed before authentication; route presence is still not live-data or mutation proof.

In-process tests prove only that the current GET targets are fixed and query input cannot choose an external target. Auth is a pre-SSR 307, notifications remains a 200 script document, and wallet management remains a pre-SSR 308; source middleware cookie, logout, session-ordering, method/cache, and browser parity remain open.
